fresh_corrections_and_qualifications.source: Stanford primer pages 10-12 and MIT transpose summary page 1
fresh_corrections_and_qualifications.verification: Complete selected-page reading and independent domain analysis
fresh_corrections_and_qualifications.finding: Real dot-product and ordinary-transpose statements must not be silently promoted to complex positivity or unrestricted one-sided inverse equivalence.
fresh_corrections_and_qualifications.correction: For complex geometry use conjugate transpose. R^T R is complex symmetric, but positivity and Hermitian Gram geometry require R*R. A left inverse implies a right inverse only for square finite-dimensional matrices; rectangular embeddings are a counterexample. Negative matrix powers require invertibility.

independent_checks: Recomputed both Stanford page-7 products and verified the printed noncommutation example exactly.
Verified symbolically both U V=I and V U=I for the unit-upper-triangular inverse. Derive V=I-N+N^2 from N^3=0 instead of copying erroneous row labels.
Checked an independent matrix-unit trace counterexample: tr(E12 E21 E11)=1 while tr(E12 E11 E21)=0. This distinguishes cyclic trace rotation from arbitrary factor permutation.
recommended_question_development: Use a rectangular product with unequal m,n,p and calculate it by entry, column, row and outer-product views; attach intermediate shapes and independently reconcile every output entry.
Construct a linear map from images of basis vectors, then compose two maps; show why factor order reverses the spoken action order and why one agreement vector does not prove map equality.
Compare a nonzero zero-divisor with a rectangular left-inverse example; state which side can be cancelled and describe the kernel direction preventing cancellation.
Extend the unit-triangular inverse type to compatible block matrices. In the top-right inverse block retain AC-B in that order; verify both block products and do not commute matrix blocks.
Contrast a real symmetric product with noncommuting symmetric factors. Prove that AB is symmetric exactly when AB=BA under the stated symmetric-square hypotheses.
Include a complex transpose-versus-adjoint example; derive Gram positivity as x* A* A x=||Ax||^2 and separate positivity from entrywise signs.
Derive selector and matrix-unit identities by entries, then use them to form minimal counterexamples to cancellation, arbitrary trace permutation and unqualified scalar binomial expansion.

For nilpotent powers provide the increasing-index-chain proof for strictly upper-triangular matrices, then obtain a finite inverse polynomial; do not replace a finite identity with an unstated convergence assumption.
Treat finite arithmetic and computational cost as separate questions: preserve factor order when optimizing parenthesization, include exact dimensions and explain rounding qualifications.

Differentiate Frobenius and induced norms if both appear in a question. The selected sources do not teach their complete general theory, so any advanced norm extension needs an independent proof or another genuinely reviewed written source.
